analysis: The PR modifies only docs/operations/provider-release.md, a documentation file. The patch excerpt shows the date bump (2026-11-12 to 2026-11-13) and a rewrite of the release-preparation paragraph (head lines 30-57): version 0.10.13 prepared as a patch over v0.10.12, with a pre-tag checklist. The checklist covers the toolchain pins, the weak-import check (scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py, matching the canonical SDK 27.2 Date comparison note), submodule pins, cluster runtime facts, catalog room (24 approvals per release, 64 limit) and a changelog.d check. I examined the base excerpts (lines 448-1107) and head lines 1-483. The unchanged release-pipeline security controls remain consistent in the head text: the tag-gated prod identity, no secrets in the dev lane, the signed-tag recheck before registration, retained-artifact retries, and no rebuild or re-sign for publication retries. The statement that pairs still on 0.10.11 stop serving until they update is an availability note, not a regression. No code, workflow, entitlement, key or trust-boundary behavior changes. No threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations are weakened. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, and the head text is shown only through line 483. The remaining head lines were not seen, but the changed ranges listed are all early in the file (head lines up to 57), so the unseen portion is likely unchanged. The claims about the v0.10.12 metallib hash and the catalog arithmetic are operational and unverifiable here, and they gate only a human pre-tag check, not a control.
